mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent FEDFUNDS increases.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which leads to wage inflation and increased corporate costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE < 4% does not correlate with subsequent wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or RSAFS growth does not correlate with subsequent earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% MoM signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO MoM < -2% does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy in a strong labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening monetary policy in strong labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of FEDFUNDS > 4% and UNRATE < 5% does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% YoY signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or HOUST YoY < -10% does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, the combination signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of PAYEMS MoM > 200,000 and UNRATE < 5% does not correlate with subsequent positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 3% YoY signals strong economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO YoY > 3% does not correlate with subsequent earnings growth.
